title: Bringing The Kingdom To The Workplace Part 1
paragraphs: I want to start with a statement that may be upsetting, but they say much of what I say upsets before it changes a person's life. I have thought about this for a long time. Therefore, what I am about to say is not a coincidence. It took me 30 years to reach this conclusion, and you can take note of that. The first task God gave to man was not worship, but work. This may be shocking, because whenever you think about Christianity, the church, or religiosity, you always think about worship.

But God's priorities are very clear in the holy books. God says that his first task is not worship, but work. In God's mind, work is a higher priority than ritual worship. Please pay close attention to my words and write them exactly as I say them. Please, I did not say that God said that work is more important than worship. But I said that based on the Bible, not on your guesswork, God placed work as a first priority for man above rituals of worship.

To make the point even clearer, there are many examples in the Bible where God directly rebukes and rejects rituals of worship, and actually tells man that he does not want these rituals of worship. He prefers something more important, which is good deeds. The foundation of the theology of work is found in the first book of the Bible, chapter one. Please read this with me. The two most important chapters in the Bible are Genesis, chapter one and chapter two.

What you will hear in the next thirty minutes will overturn your theology, and perhaps shake your deeply held convictions about what is important to God. The emphasis the Creator placed on work is evident from the priority He gave it even in the Sabbath law. In fact, there are people who spend so much time focusing on Saturday that they forget the task assigned to them for the next six days. How am I doing so far?

Some people are so particular about one day of the week that they forget the purpose of the rest of the week. We will correct that this week. Let us read what the Creator Himself tells us. Genesis, Chapter 1, Verse 26. God said, “Let us make mankind in our image and likeness, so that they may attend churches, form choirs, and hold worship sessions, so that God may be pleased as God.” Because God gets depressed when no one tells Him how great He is. This is roughly how we arrive at our theological position.

But God does not say that. This is the first statement God makes about our mission on Earth. "To have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over all the earth, and over all the creeping things that creep upon the earth." So God created man. Verse 27: In his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them. God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over it.” Chapter Two.

I'm going to read something that will shock you. Chapter two begins in this way. The heavens and the earth were perfected in all their splendor and majesty. The second verse, on the seventh day, God had finished. Please underline the word work whenever you see it. God had finished the work he was doing. So he rested on the seventh day from all the work he had done. And God blessed and sanctified the seventh day, because on it he rested from all his work which he had done, creating all that he had created.

The concept of work was introduced in the second chapter of the Bible. There are no demons, no devil, no darkness, no sin, no broken homes, no persecution, no depression, no stress. However, there is work to be done in this chapter. In a way, Christians believed that work was a result of the fall of man. But the work was submitted before you fell. The first person to follow this approach was not a human being. But it was God. God could not do anything He wanted without action.

God worked so hard that he had to rest. You should never rest until you have worked hard. Now this is interesting. God says: " Six days you work, and everyone cheers for me." Six days a week. How many days? All of you raise six fingers. Let everyone say: "Is this the amount?" Six days a week. How many days do you rest? Raise one finger. Let everyone say this is how comfortable you are. Now let's see how smart you are.

If I asked you to do something six times and then you did something else once, which is more important to me? The thing I asked you to do six times. God's worth in terms of value is demonstrated by the number of times He has commanded you to do something. The average person—and I would have said Bahamian, but this is an international television broadcast—the average person would prefer to work one day a week and rest for six. God knew that things would come to this. Therefore, prioritize first.

He said you will work six days and rest for only one day. God's priority. Therefore, in this simple principle alone, work is more important than rest in the eyes of God. Now here's something a little deeper. Get your Bible and underline these words. This is amazing. Verse 5, Chapter 2. Now nothing of the bushes of the wilderness, listen to this, had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any grass of the wilderness sprouted, because the Lord God had not yet allowed rain on the earth. Look at me for a moment.

What does this phrase mean? Use your logic. This means that the seeds were present. Is anyone listening to me? In other words, the plant, shrub, and grass were already there. All she needed was rainwater. But the text says that God did not allow it to rain because if He had, it would have brought life to the planet. Read the following phrase, my brother. It's amazing. It is in the Bible. God says that He did not allow the rain because there was no human being to do it. Oh, my God. Let me simplify it a little.

What is this chapter about? the second. No demons, no devils, no darkness, no sin. God says, "I need someone who does not worship, does not sing, does not clap, does not light candles, does not burn incense, does not attend prayer meetings, does not fast or pray." He says, "I need a human being to work." I don't know if you understood the message. There is no church in the first two chapters. I got a little ahead of myself. There is no choir in chapters one and two.

There are no prayer meetings in chapters one and two. There is no fasting in the first and second chapters. There are no massacres, no sacrifices, no blood, no incense, nothing. In that chapter, God concludes his words by saying, "This is very good." Are you trying to say that what we are doing now is not very good? The answer should be yes. This is not good. What are we doing? We need to gather in certain places. We need a cheerleader called a worship singer to make us sing.

We need musical instruments and drums to stir our emotions so that we can raise our hands and praise the Lord. We need someone to deliver an inspiring and exciting message to tickle our emotions so that we can cheer a little. In other words, God got fed up with all these acrobatic moves and all the programs that prepare us, because there was none of that in Heaven. And God said, " This is very good." Yes.

But according to what was in heaven, there was no worship service, no priest, no preacher, no messenger, no evangelist. There was no choir member. However, the Bible says that man used to walk and talk with God in the daytime breeze. He didn't need to set the mood. He did n't need organ music to make things go well. He did not need a candle, nor the scent of incense to feel holy. He would simply walk among the croton plants and talk amidst the hibiscus flowers. Something went wrong. Why did God create him?

I asked you the question from your own holy book. It's there. God says I needed someone to do the work. I asked the priests everywhere I traveled. I was in Brazil, and Dr. Kintajali is here tonight. He was with me there two weeks ago. I stood before 11,000 priests and asked them a question. I said, "Why did God create us?" And most Christians answered, "To worship." That's not true. If God wanted to be worshipped, He would have enough angels to do it. Now, don't misunderstand me.

We'll correct this shortly because what you call worship isn't worship. Jesus told the religious people of his time, who were doing everything correctly, "You worship me with your lips, but your hearts are so far from what I intended that you disgust me." You are like the bones of the dead in a whitewashed cemetery. O snakes. I mean, he rebuked those religious people who practice worship. Why? Because it's not about attending church on Sunday. What matters is what you do on Monday. Can we read that again?

Because some of you seem shocked. It is in the Bible. Let's read it. God did not allow any shrub to grow because there was no human being to work the land. Now, I like this because God tells us what's on his mind. He does not think about church services or prayer meetings. What is he thinking about? the job. So, as he was forming the human, he was thinking: I've got a worker here. As he blew on the man, he said: I'm getting a worker for myself here. Let everyone say: "I was born to work." I was born to work.

Verse seven. Then the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground. And he breathed into his nostrils a breath of life, and man became a living soul. Say it aloud. Say "work" together. aloud. Work. I want you to work on this word for a few minutes. Come on everyone, say "do it". Work. Work on it. Let's go. Say it, do it. Work. Hit your neighbor. Say: "Work". Work. Hit them hard again. Say: "Work". Get your work done. Say: "Get your work done." Get your work done. Hit them again. Say: "Work".

I want you to clap your hands because you are now receiving correction from God. I want you to applaud and open your mouths. While you applaud, cheer a little. That's good. Tell your neighbor that he is reading it correctly. Then go to work. Can you say something else to me in a very loud voice? Hit your neighbor. Say: Go to work, you lazy worshipper. Hallelujah. God created man from the dust of the earth. He breathed into it a breath of life, and it became a living soul. Now, let's read. Now, I will not read it.

I'm going to leave you with some assignments this week, but I want you to take a look at some of the things that happened after that. God began to speak, and he spoke to this man. Listen to what he says to the man. He says: "The Lord planted a garden." Verse eight, and he begins to talk about this paradise. He says, "In heaven, there are all kinds of trees." Verse nine is pleasing to the eye. Why? Because he sent the rain. Why? He got a worker for himself.

Do you know why God did not allow it to grow until man came? Because God wanted someone to plant, organize, and maintain. Let everyone say: "The administration". Administration. Say it out loud. I can't hear you. Say it louder. You were created to manage planet Earth, not the heavens. God hates jungles. I'll say this again. God hates jungles. The term "jungle" refers to unregulated, undeveloped, and uncultivated land. Let everyone look at me. Look at me.

The most beautiful hotel in the entire Caribbean region today is located in the Bahamas. It is called Atlantis. You will pay me for this advertisement. They spent over $200 million. On a rocky piece no more than two miles wide and about two and a half miles long. Do you know what we used to call that rock to which the island was pulled? I want you to learn a lesson here. We have been monitoring that island. We were dumping garbage there. We used to put wild boars there. Everyone was making fun of that island.

They described it as filthy and useless. We used to make fun of that island. We named it Pig Island. But who would have thought that where there was filth is now where horses roam? Why? Because a man looked into the jungle. Come on, everyone. He said, "I have a dream." But it requires... I can't hear you right now. You must answer me loudly for international television. Let's go. It requires you to see the Bahamian. He was not ready for work. They are my people. I can talk to them. You, the visitors.

They were not prepared to pay the price of sacrificing for work. It's not about the money. Believe me, it's the vision. God never said that people perish because they lack money. And I am living proof of that. This is correct. It's the vision. God says, "I don't want jungles." I want a creature that walks through the jungle and sees a building with five hundred rooms that does not yet exist. The dog cannot do that. The cat cannot do that. The bird cannot do that.

I need a creature that resembles me, that can see things that don't exist as if they do. But it requires work. the job. Then God tells man about gold, silver, oil, resin, and the ox. These are precious stones, diamonds. Then verse 15: Then the Lord God took the man and put him in the garden and said, “Work.” It's best if you listen to me carefully. My sermon is over. The first thing God did was work. His work produced work. Therefore, man was made to work. And so man was given work. Let me say this.

The word Aden, our members know this, but you will get a different perspective. Write the word Aden now, everyone. Where did God take man and place him? In Aden. Aden is not a name. It is a Hebrew word meaning spot or moment. It also means the present moment or the moment of his presence somewhere. Listen, God took man and put him in paradise, a Hebrew word that indicates his presence. Don't miss this. When God took man and placed him in His presence, what did He tell him to do? the job. Will you understand?

The purpose of attending is for work. Now when you lose attendance, you get disrupted. Stay with me. The reason you hold a mass, pray, sing, and offer sacrifices is that you are trying to recover what you lost in the second chapter, which is his presence. And when you regain his presence, you go to work. Some of you will realize that after we're done. You think that attendance is just to sit there and say, "Oh, priest, this looks great." Go to work. The swab is for work. His presence is for work purposes.

If you do not feel like working, start with worship. When His presence comes, you should feel a desire to work, not to worship. Worship brings his presence so that you can go to work. If it was Sunday, then I understand, don't I? If Sunday was your day to get his presence and you got a good dose, prove it on Monday. Come on, clap your hands, people. You go to work to prove that you have his presence. That's why when you go to the workplace, people are supposed to sense his presence around you.

I like what Jesus said when he came to set things right. He says, “Let your light shine so brightly before the people in the marketplace, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father. Now then, clap your hands, people!” You see, that's the main purpose of getting an attendance. Let everyone say: "Worship for the sake of work." Worship for the sake of work. We love to be immersed in the spirit. We like to be wiped. We like to feel what we call the power of God.

But when you read the Bible, you find that every manifestation of God's power was because there was work to be done. David did not receive the power of God to sit on a rock and play the harp. There was work that needed to be done. Hello, is anyone here? There was a giant in the city making a lot of noise, so David said, "I have to go to work." So he took his tool, which is called a slingshot. He placed some smooth stones in it. He said, "I'm going to work." He said to Goliath, "I have come to work."

The liar said, "Your tools are not good enough." He said, "Well, I am in his presence. When I am in his presence, the tools work. And God placed man in Paradise and said, ' What?'" "Get to work. Let me give you some statistics. I have 10 minutes. 70%—this is a statistic from the University of California about work among Christians. This is tough. A college in London also conducted a study on Christian attitudes toward work. We spend 70% of our daily lives at work. Write that down somewhere.

Write that down somewhere. 70 % of your day is spent at work. 70%. The second statistic: 50% of Christians have never heard a sermon about work. 50%. This means that if you met two Christians, one of them would never have heard a sermon about work. The third statistic: 70% of Christians have not been taught the theology of work. 70% of pastors have never sat down with a teacher to learn the theology of work.

This means that 70% of Christians have no biblical convictions or foundation for spending 70% of their lives at work. Now you understand why people think the only way to do something good for God is to quit your job and become a preacher or pastor. Because the theology taught in the church sees that you're not doing that." Something good for God unless you're a preacher. What a mess in biblical theology! According to Genesis chapters 1 and 2, God has given us 100% responsibility for work.

A fourth statistic shocked me: 70% have never been preached about their profession. 70% of the world's Christians, according to one study, have never heard a sermon about their career. Can you imagine going to a place where you spend 70% of the day and you don't believe that's God's will? No wonder you hate your job and your boss. We don't take the Kingdom of God to the workplace. We just take a stand. Come on, sit up straight for the last few minutes. Look, we go to work saying, "Oh, Monday's here again."

Don't say anything to me. "I don't feel well today." I mean, you just left church on Sunday night shouting and clapping, and on Monday you tell the sinner, "Don't say anything to me." You were supposed to say something to them. But you see, the theology the church has been promoting makes you hate the place where you spend most of your life. Another statistic that shocked me: less than 25% of Christians have been asked about their work witness by their pastor, minister, or priest. That's a statistic from the study.

Less than 25% have ever been asked about their work witness by their minister. Why? Because ministers don't think it matters at all. One last statistic I gleaned from the study that you might find interesting is that only 26% of Christians have been asked to develop a workplace ministry. Only 26% have been asked to do something in their workplace to influence it for the sake of God's kingdom. 26%. That means 74% are convinced that work is just a nuisance.

Work has been marginalized by the general congregation through a belief encapsulated in a phrase, which I've written down. From the book On the Last Day. The phrase says, “All Christians are born equal, but full-time Christians are more equal than others.” This is the belief held by most Christians. Let me say it again. We were taught in church that all Christians are born equal, but full-time Christians, those engaged in full Christian service, are more equal than the rest. What a pathetic perception we have.

In other words, the implication is that if you want to do something for God, you must leave your job, your career, or whatever you love or are paid to do, and you must come and become a full-time Christian worker. This is unbiblical. It is diabolical because it literally destroys God’s people’s chances of winning the world. In fact, I am deeply sorry, Mr.

Minister, because it still bothers me that you stood here tonight as a man in a position that influences legislation and sets policies for my country, and affects my grandchildren. And you have to apologize to me as a man of God because you quoted the Bible. I repent, my brother. I am sorry. Forgive me. But why does he feel this way? Because we believe that you cannot be a politician and a Christian at the same time. And the church taught him that.

I am glad you are here, politicians, because I came to tell you, my brother, this is not just a job for you. You were born to do this. This is your anointing. God created you to do what you do. Never call it a job. It is your work. And I will say to you now, in front of the world, my brother, you are the Minister of Housing and you are in my cabinet. But I tell you, my brother, you have the same anointing that I have to do what I was born to do, just as I was born to do what I was born to do.

Let everyone say: Work. Work. The church is at fault. Let me quote something that may be of interest to you. The workplace is God's place. Say it with me. The workplace is the land that belongs to the Lord, not the church building. Lord, I mean right now. The earth and all that is in it belongs to the Lord. IBM, AT&T, SuperValue, whatever your workplace is, it belongs to the Lord.

This means that when you walk into that store on a Monday morning, you are walking into a place that belongs to God, and they are paying you to witness and give evidence. With your life, your punctuality, and your excellent work. You don't want to answer me because it's a little late, but you might want to cheer just once, because we need to stop thinking that worship only starts on Sunday. Let me tell you something. Worship starts on Monday. Ah, I have another quote. Quick, quick. Look, God is at work.

I'm reading the Bible. God is working in us. God is working through us, and God is working in those who work with us. I was created to work. Repeat after me. I was created to work. Repeat it again. I was created to work. Raise your right hands in the air and say it. I wanted these words to go right into your souls. I was created to work. Raise them again and pass them on to your cousin, your uncle, and your aunt. Buy this tape and give it to all your employees. Come on, say it. I was created to work. God says so.

Please clap with those hands you just raised. The church has been engaged in the mission of evangelization for over The past two thousand years. But its concept of evangelism has been tainted because it has been reduced to mass preaching, preaching from the porch, and preaching in the streets. But thank God, the 21st-century church is returning to its essence. We are returning to our roots and will practice what I call action evangelism.

We will be that salt you speak of, influencing the workplace and transforming it into a kingdom. You know, while we work on the periphery, we forget the center. We spend more time at work than anywhere else. Listen to the statistics again. Seventy percent of a person's working life is spent at work. Didn't you hear me? Not with your children. Not in your homes. But in that place you go.

This means that if you don't see the workplace as a place God has set aside to influence the kingdom, then you are working as a Christian and bearing witness for only 30 percent of your life. What a tragedy. We spend more time at work than in the homes we have built with our labor. My father is here tonight. I love my father. He is almost 77 years old. He has worked his whole life to build us a home.

And when we see people like my father who worked his whole life to build a house, and by the time the mortgage is due, they can't even climb a single step into it, why? Seventy percent of their lives were given to earning money to build that place they can't even enter. What a tragedy. We need to change our mindset. We need a new baptism, like Genesis chapters 1 and 2. We need to understand that Monday is the moment of truth. It's not just a choir hymn, incense you smell, and a few sermons.

My friend, it happens when you sit behind a typewriter, or hold a hammer, or a wrench in your hand, so people can see what God looks like amidst the grease of work. You should applaud here. I want to challenge someone from this conference to write a book called "God in the Grease of Work." We need God dressed as a nurse and a police officer. We need God walking around in hotel service uniforms. We need God in work clothes. Tell your neighbors, "Go to work." " We're going to have a lot of fun this week.

The workplace is a natural place to find the lost. I'm amazed. Lord, listen. Just give me two more minutes. We, we go looking for the lost. Hmm, just go to work. Come on, clap your hands, everyone. Our church goes preaching, son. We're going to walk around that neighborhood. We're going to go looking for the lost. You go to them every Monday morning. In fact, you surround them. They're a crowd trapped at work. They have to come back. Lord, have mercy. Do you get that, brother?

If I start preaching on Monday and I don't finish, no problem. I can see you in the morning and start on Tuesday and I don't finish. No problem. You come back on Wednesday, and I still haven't finished. No problem. When I'm done with you, I go looking for the lost. God sent you where they are, and they pay you to stay. Come on, clap your hands, everyone. Let everyone say: Work. The workplace is a restricted mission field. The workplace is the perfect stage to show your faith.

We are encouraged to go fishing in The ponds and swamps while we sit on a lake full of fish. That's called work. The holiest field of mission is the workplace. That's why God gave you that job. I'm concluding now. Look, you think God gave you that job because you wanted a paycheck. God gave you the job because He wants people in that company to experience His grace and good love. That's why He sent you. But your church messed it up.

Did you know that the church convinced society not to let you bear witness at your workplace? The church community encourages us to believe that our faith is a private matter and that there's no place for your faith at work. Where did they get that idea? From the church. This prejudice against Christianity leads to a fear of not fitting in at work. So we keep quiet. But consider the lives of God's most effective witnesses in this book.

I'm going to ask you, who was the most effective in the Old Testament at winning over the nations? Who? Let me give you some names, and then tell me if they were pastors, apostles, prophets, or preachers. These are the most effective. Let me give you a big shock before I give you their names. I'm going to tell you Who weren't the most effective witnesses? Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, Joel. These weren't active witnesses. They were prophets who wrote books and spoke to Israel.

The most effective witnesses—what is a witness? Not the people who preached to the church. Don't miss this point. Isaiah preached to the church, Israel. Joel preached to the church, Israel. Ezra preached to the church, Israel. But when God wanted to reach the world—come on, don't miss this— He chose people like Joseph. You know Job? Joseph. Joseph wasn't a shepherd or a prophet or a preacher or an evangelist. Joseph was the deputy prime minister. He spoke to me. I say, he spoke to me.

And he didn't leave his job to bear witness for God. The purpose of his job was to bear witness for God. And God used this deputy prime minister to change the religious laws of the entire nation. Pharaoh worshipped the sun. But when he met Joseph— come on, folks—and Joseph, in his role, revealed the kingdom of God. The pagan Pharaoh who worshipped the sun issued a decree throughout the land, changed the constitution, and ordered every Egyptian to worship a god. Joseph, Jehovah, Jehovah.

You'd better applaud, everyone. Where did this happen? In... I ca n't hear you. This happened at his workplace. How about a second example? Daniel. Who wasn't a Gentile? Daniel. That's right. What was Daniel? A permanent secretary in the government. Oh, you hear about Daniel in the lions' den and what Daniel did. No, no. He wasn't a preacher, brother. He was just like you. He worked for the government. He was a politician. God used Daniel to change an entire nation. Nebuchadnezzar worshipped demons.

Nebuchadnezzar boiled babies in milk and fried them in blood. He was one of those Gentiles who followed a corrupt religion. But he met a man in a high position who kept his job. And do you know why he admired Daniel? Not because Daniel said " Hallelujah" at work. Not because Daniel read his Bible at the desk when it should have been printed. Not because Daniel held prayer meetings in the bathhouse. But the Bible says, "Oh, my God, come on, preacher. Can you help me a little?"

It says the king said Regarding Daniel, this man was always punctual. I'm quoting the Bible. He never took a longer lunch break than necessary. He worked longer hours than expected. He did a better job than all his colleagues. And he had an excellent spirit. And in his workplace, by the way, stand up for your faith in the workplace. When they tell you that you can't do this or that, or ask you to do things that go against your citizenship in the Kingdom, stand firm. They threaten to fire you. They will demote you.

They will hold you back. But I want you to leave this conference with a new anointing to tell them: You didn't give me this job. And you can't take it away from me. And before I leave, I will go into the lions' den and come out unscathed, and you will be saved just like me. You must applaud once before we go home. When Daniel finished, the Bible says that the king said, "Daniel, this God of yours has saved you from the lions' den."

I will now promote you, not from assistant secretary to secretary, but you will now become an assistant to the king, and we will announce the destruction of all statues and idols in our country and we will write a new law. Can you all hear me? We will make every Babylonian worship the god of the working man. Tell your neighbor, with a firm hint, to get to work. Go to work and continue with your work. I want you to return to work tomorrow, to Parliament and to the Ministry. I tell you, my brother.

I want you to go in there. Tell everyone that I am anointed and appointed by God. The people did not elect you, my brother. God has put them in a position of power so that you can do things for Him. There are certain policies that God wants to achieve. There are some laws that God wants to reform. God wants you to protect the poor. He wants you to take care of those in need. He wants you to care for the needy. He says, "I'm going to rub you with oil." That is your invitation, my brother. Do your job, man.

Do your job. This is not politics, my friend. This is your spiritual service. Promotion does not come from the East, nor from the West, nor from the North, but it comes from God. My brother, there were three Hebrew youths who, as the book says, were assistant ministers. They changed the entire country through their jobs. Nehemiah, oh. Oh. Nehemiah was a cupbearer of wine. Come on, talk to me. Don't make things complicated. He was a cupbearer in the king's court. He did not quit his job.

He changed the world through his work. We don't want another preacher to spoil the spiritual service. Stay where you are. Stay a carpenter or a nurse. Stay in that mechanical job. That's your service. Bring the kingdom into the world of law. Bring the kingdom into the business world. Bring the Kingdom into the world of education. The king said: Nehemiah, why is your heart so downcast? He said: Because I don't like the appearance of the neighborhood; the walls are broken and the people are unemployed.

I have an idea. If we start building the wall, we will keep people busy. You will not have an unemployment problem. The king said, " I liked your idea." When Nehemiah proposed that plan, some of you thought the king was a fool. The king said, “This man is a businessman. He’s a politician. This man can provide jobs for the people. My biggest problem is these illiterate and undisciplined Jews. This man will create a project to employ them. That’s good policy. How many speeches do you need?”

He said, “ Clap your hands, people!” “Ji,” the man was clever. He said, “If I give this man this task, he will create more jobs.” And the Bible says the people were willing to work. The king was credited with building a wall started by a man who was a bartender and didn’t quit his job. Tell your neighbor, “Go to work.” Or, “Stay in your job.” The church is to blame for neglecting to bring the kingdom into the workplace. The church focuses on living one day a week and neglects the wisdom of the other six.

Most pastors prepare their congregations solely for church service. Ministries centered around the skills and talents of ministers make people think that the only way to do God’s will is to serve in the church. And the church calls that our leader. And I want to conclude by talking about Jesus. Lord, have mercy. I love Him very much. Would you like to hear something, Bishop? Jesus, our leader. Ah, that was amazing. Look, most pastors unintentionally prepare people to support only their own ministries.

Well, Pastor, sit down properly.
